title: Existence of an invariant measure & Feller property (title is 'Unique Ergodicity')

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
The problem is *unique ergodicity* = existence AND uniqueness, but the original 'Proof of Main Result' establishes only uniqueness ('no more than one invariant measure'). The solution.tex adds a Krylov-Bogolyubov argument (paragraph 'Existence of an invariant measure'). Two genuine gaps there:

1. **Feller property asserted from a pointwise semigroup limit.** The argument states: 'P is Feller on E (it is the pointwise limit of the Feller semigroups P^m)'. A pointwise limit of Feller maps need NOT be Feller: it need not map C_b -> C_b nor preserve continuity. Krylov-Bogolyubov requires P to be Feller. Moreover, even for a FIXED smooth h (as in the problem statement), the Feller property — continuous dependence of Law(u_t) on u_0 in C_0([0,1]) — is used but never justified.

2. **Uniform-in-time spatial Holder bound.** The claim sup_{t>=0} E||u_t||_{C^{1/9}} <= C (eq. holder-unif) is obtained by re-running the spatial-Holder estimate on each [n,n+1] started from u_n, using ||P_a f||_{C^{1/9}} <= ||f||_{C^{1/9}}. But the restart decomposition u_t = P_{t-n}u_n + (drift over [n,t]) + (V_t - P_{t-n}V_n) and the n-INDEPENDENCE of the Gaussian+drift contributions are only sketched. A genuine uniform moment/regularity bound (constants independent of n) is needed for tightness of the time-averages bar-mu_T.

Suggested fix: (a) scope to fixed smooth h and prove Feller directly via continuous dependence on initial data (same heat-kernel/SSL machinery, Lipschitz-in-u_0 of the mild map); (b) prove the uniform Holder bound with explicit n-independent constants (Gaussian part: Ito isometry + hypercontractivity; drift part: c:310 with T-S<=1; P_{t-n}u_n: contraction in C^{1/9}); then KB with the compact embedding C^{1/9} cap C_0 -> C_0. For the singular m->infty limit, 'Feller of the limit semigroup' coincides in difficulty with the mollifier-limit gap (prob-05-8).
